merge.title: Verify-before-first-power tool plus a host-verified birth record, with each leg scoped to the attacker it actually stops (MCU attestation demoted to an optional post-enrolment die-identity check)
merge.threat:
Transit or reseller interdiction of a unit that ships debug-open at RDP-0, plus contract-manufacturer overbuild and clones. Invariant #10(a) rests on the buyer verifying before first power, but the only tool is an operator script against a bench profile that reads option bytes and named flash hashes only (tools/verify_ship_state.py:84-100,134-157), and the ship profile is an unfillable template. Over USB the companion is origin-blind: FW_VERSION is a fixed 3.0.0, device_uid is 16 zero bytes, the USB serial is "0001" and no attestation command exists.

Attacker ladder and the leg that answers each:
- A1, reflash or option-byte, OTP or per-device-page tamper at RDP-0: stopped by leg 1 (external dump diff). This is the only leg that is unconditional on factory honesty.
- A2, planted OEM1/OEM2 regression key: detected by leg 1 (NSSR lock bits) and neutralised by leg 2 (overwrite at the RDP burn).
- A3, CM overbuild, clone boards without genuine SEs, UID re-use, single SE swapped against the factory record: stopped by leg 3 (signed manifest, log, SE vendor attestation, per-element binding). Conditional on factory record and log honesty.
- A4, re-bagging or bag swap by a low-tier attacker: leg 4 (bag serial in OTP).
- A5, whole-device lookalike swap after enrolment, with no live relay: optional leg 5.
- Not stopped by any leg: an SWD-emulating fake MCU carrying transplanted genuine SEs on day one; genuine chips on a hostile PCB or a display, button or I2C implant; a relay to the stolen genuine unit; a malicious signed firmware update.
merge.proposal:
One design, five legs in priority order. Only leg 1 is P0.

**Leg 1 (P0, host tooling, no firmware): `pq1-verify`.**
- Read-only, connect-under-reset; refuse any write verb (keep the WRITE_VERBS allow-list).
- Read set:
  - both flash banks, diffed against the reproducible release;
  - every option-byte register (OPTR, SECBOOTADD0, SECWM1/2, WRP1A/B and WRP2A/B, BOOT_LOCK, HDP, BOR_LEV);
  - FLASH_NSSR OEM1LOCK/OEM2LOCK, which must be clear;
  - the OTP programmed-quad-word map — a map, not a digest, because OTP is per-unit and holds the secret transport master at bytes 128..160; compare locally, never upload or log it;
  - the 96-bit UID at 0x0BFA_0700 (the address the code uses, not the 0x0BFA_0590 in the docs);
  - DBGMCU_IDCODE;
  - per-device pages 123..127, which must be blank;
  - TAMP backup registers, recorded as advisory only.
- Output: green plus the 8 fingerprint words the device will show, or red with the differing region.
- Ship as a single binary plus a WebUSB (CMSIS-DAP) page plus a quickstart card.
- Release descriptor: per-slot digests, the FSBL digest (needs #742) and the ship option-byte profile.
- State the guarantee precisely: NRST is held so no instruction executes. It is not literally "before power".
- The read-set extension and packaging can land now against the bench profile. The ship profile waits on #540, #753, #39, #37 and #46.

**Leg 2 (P1, firmware, `rdp2-self-lock` only): OEM key overwrite.**
- In first-boot Phase A, write OEM1KEYR1/2 and OEM2KEYR1/2 = 0xFFFFFFFF in the same OPTSTRT as RDP=0xCC, mirroring Trezor.
- Pin the OEM-lock register and bits on a sacrificial RDP-0 board (#46/#387) and flip `OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED`.

**Leg 3 (P1, factory process plus small firmware): birth record.**
- Per unit, an HSM-signed manifest: MCU UID, OPTIGA E0C2 UID, sha256 of the E0E0 certificate, SE050 UID, ship-profile id, release and FSBL hash, bag serial, and a hash of the non-secret OTP words only.
- Append to a public transparency log, with tuple uniqueness enforced by verifiers.
- Verification is host-side only (`pq1-verify` and the companion). No on-device P-256 or SLH-DSA verifier and no boot-time permanent lockdown.
- Firmware adds only readers and relays: OPTIGA E0C2 read plus E0F0 challenge-sign, SE050 UID plus attested read.
- Host rule: each proof is verified against its own root set, and the UID tuple must be identical across the proofs and the log entry. Ship a negative test: a valid OPTIGA proof presented in another slot must fail.
- Use SHA-256, not #249's SHA3-256.

**Leg 4 (P2): bag serial.**
- One OTP quad-word holding unit and bag serial, read by `pq1-verify`.
- Shown on the existing secure-world lock-confirm page (`build_lock_confirm_pages`), not by the FSBL.

**Leg 5 (P3, optional, owner decision): `CMD_ATTEST`.**
- Per-die C10 key derived on demand from CMAC_DHUK(label ‖ page-127 salt), with derivation refused below RDP-2 and a separate KDF label.
- Signs only prefixed host challenges; enrolled by the owner's verifier (trust on first use).
- Claims die identity after enrolment only. It makes no firmware claim and no day-one genuineness claim.
- Gate behind on-device confirm or a rate limit: about 10 s per challenge, and it is a new NS-callable signing surface.

**Also (S-size fix).** Replace the GET_DEVICE_INFO placeholders with the real build hash. Whether any stable per-unit id is exposed before unlock is an owner privacy decision.

dropped_parts: USB-05 factory-issued C10 certificate over the DHUK-derived attestation pubkey, stored in a factory-written page. Infeasible: DHUK is an ST constant at RDP-0 and per-die only after the field self-lock (secure/src/main.rs:760-763; #249 body), so the factory never sees the key. A factory-written per-device page also violates Phase A's blank-page rule (PerDevicePageNotBlank 0x080B, secure/src/first_boot/state.rs:80-82).

IMP-07 and USB-05 claim that MCU attestation stops a day-one counterfeit, fake MCU or interposer. Refuted in round 1: a fake MCU enrols its own key, and everything readable at RDP-0 is copyable, including the OTP transport master.
IMP-07 claim that the manifest stops a Frankenstein PCB. Nothing binds to the PCB; three genuine chips on a hostile board pass every proof.

USB-05 fw_measurement inside the attestation signature as a firmware proof. Round-1 fact (d): any secure image can select DHUK through SAES KEYSEL, so the measurement is self-reported. A real binding needs an FSBL-hidden (HDP) secret (#39, open) and FSBL budget.

#249-style on-device boot ceremony: secure world verifies NXP/Infineon ECDSA chains plus the SLH-DSA manifest and permanently locks down on mismatch. Self-verification is worth nothing against interdiction (tools/verify_ship_state.py:8-19); it puts a classical verifier and a second PQ verifier in firmware (invariant #5 tension, slot budget); and it adds a brick path. Replaced by host-side verification.
#249 'DHUK probe via SAES against factory-recorded value'. Impossible; the same issue says the factory never runs at RDP>=1.
IMP-07 sha256(otp_area‖salt) in the public log. OTP 128..160 is the secret transport master (secure/src/hw/otp.rs:28,45-48). Hash only non-secret words.

BOOT-04 and IMP-07 FSBL-rendered bag serial. The FSBL cannot light the pq1 panel (#705), the FSBL budget is the recorded NO-GO, and the linker is still 32 KiB (#540). An RDP-0 FSBL display is also self-report. Moved to the secure-world lock-confirm page.

IMP-02 (c) PDN-impedance tier as a consumer feature. Needs a VNA and an opened case; the PA8-gated SE rail is invisible without a probe point; per-batch golden sets are unvalidated; the golden set comes from the project, so it is not factory-independent. Kept only as a P2 research note.
IMP-02 (d) 'baseline recorded by the buyer is unconditional on factory honesty' as an answer to transit interdiction. A buyer baseline postdates transit; it detects later evil-maid tamper only.
IMP-02 'TAMP backup registers expected erased' as a hard check. The board mandates a 0.47-1 F supercap (hardware_requirements.md:139-149). Advisory only.
IMP-07 rationale 'strictly better than Trezor' on the MCU leg. Trezor's key is factory-certified and does catch a day-one fake MCU; pq1 trades that for having no factory-held secret.
USB-05 UID96 as device_uid or USB serial by default. A stable identifier readable by any host or WebHID page before unlock; not adopted without an owner decision.

user-device-verification.md work item 3 (confirm-gated Phase A). Already implemented in the candidate: secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:219-240 (confirm_checked, then rdp_burn_authorized), under rdp2-self-lock.

merge.precedent:
**Attestation legs are parity.**
- Trezor Safe 7 ships an ML-DSA-44 MCU leg: the key is regenerated per sign from a flash-stored seed, with a factory-issued certificate passed in startup args (core/embed/sec/mcu_attestation/mcu_attestation.c:63-97; smcall wrappers at core/embed/sys/smcall/stm32/smcall_verifiers.c:237-286).
- trezorlib enforces same root, serial and common name across chains (python/src/trezorlib/authentication.py:673-698).
- Ledger Genuine Check uses an SE-held key with HSM challenge-response.
- Trezor resets the OEM keys to 0xFFFFFFFF and checks NSSR OEMxLOCK every boot (option_bytes.c:213-222, 247-250).
- Coldcard records the bag number in the device and shows it at first power.

**The verifier is beyond parity.** No wallet vendor ships a user-run pre-power flash, option-byte and OTP verifier. Trezor's nearest tool is the host-side verify_signed_firmware.py, a byte-diff against the reproducible build, with no SWD step.

PDN impedance (PDNPulse, TIFS 2023) and Purism/Star Labs photo baselines are non-wallet precedents for the research tier.
merge.rationale:
The whole post-sale trust story (invariant #10) assumes a buyer-side check that does not exist for any buyer. Leg 1 is host-only, costs no flash, and is the single defence that does not depend on the factory, so it carries the P0. Its read-set and packaging part is M-size and can start now; the ship profile is blocked on other owners.

The attestation material from IMP-07 and USB-05 is mostly #249 restated. Its distinctive MCU leg cannot do what was claimed under ship-at-RDP-0, so it is kept only where it is sound:
- host-verified SE vendor attestation plus a signed, logged UID tuple, for overbuild, clones and UID re-use;
- an optional post-enrolment die-identity check at P3.

Cost L is for the whole bundle. Leg 1 alone is M, leg 2 is S, leg 3 is L (factory HSM, log operation, SE plumbing), leg 4 is S, leg 5 is M.

Novelty is 'beyond' only for the pre-power verifier. Every attestation leg is parity with Trezor and Ledger and should not be marketed otherwise.

merge.residual_after:
What an attacker can still do once all five legs land:
1. **Fake MCU on day one.** A counterfeit board with an SWD-emulating fake MCU plus the victim unit's transplanted genuine SEs serves genuine bytes, a copied UID and copied OTP to `pq1-verify`, passes SE vendor attestation and the log lookup, and enrols its own leg-5 key. There is no cryptographic detector under ship-at-RDP-0; only tamper evidence and per-unit cost stand in the way. This is the residual already accepted at user-device-verification.md:169-175.
2. **Board-level implants.** Genuine chips on a hostile PCB, or an implant on the display SPI, buttons or SE I2C, pass every leg. That is other clusters' scope. The PDN tier would at best catch PDN-powered additions on the main rail.
3. **SWD interposer.** An interposer on PA13/PA14, or a compromised buyer probe or host, can present clean flash. Partly mitigated by an independently sourced probe and by comparing tool words, screen words and published words, which itself needs #705 fixed.
4. **Malicious factory or log operator.** Either can sign and log a bad tuple. Legs 3 and 4 are conditional on them; only leg 1's firmware-bytes claim is not.
5. **Bag serial.** It is printed on the bag, and blank OTP is writable at RDP-0, so an attacker who replaces the die and re-prints a bag defeats leg 4. It stops only casual re-bagging.
6. **Leg 5 limits.** It proves die identity, not firmware: a malicious signed update or a glitched secure image on the same die signs any challenge. A lookalike device relaying the challenge to the stolen genuine unit also passes. It gives nothing before enrolment.
7. **Unverified units.** A buyer who skips leg 1, or cannot reach SWD on a sealed unit, gets none of the unconditional guarantee.
8. **Snapshot only.** Leg 1 says nothing about tamper after the check and before the RDP-2 lock, beyond the "keep the device in hand" procedure.

skeptic.reason:
The core survives: an off-device, read-only, connect-under-reset verifier is the only check that means anything at RDP-0, and it does not exist for any buyer. tools/verify_ship_state.py:134-157 reads only option bytes and named flash hashes, the only checkable profile is the bench one, and docs/security/user-device-verification.md:3 says nothing is implemented. Demoting MCU attestation and moving manifest verification host-side is consistent with the ship-at-RDP-0 decision and invariant #5. The tracked-issue list is accurate as far as it goes; every number I checked is open with the stated subject.

The recommendation is not refuted, but it needs these fixes before it is banked:

1. **Leg 2 builds on a burn routine that is known to be inert.** secure/src/hw/flash.rs:384-394 records defect #268: the RDP-2 burn writes OPTSTRT/OBL_LAUNCH to FLASH_SECCR, where those bits do not exist, so it returns Ok without burning. The merge cites #268 only as "first-boot provisioning".
2. **The OEM-lock bit positions in the code are wrong, and can be corrected from in-tree vendor files today.** shared/src/lockdown.rs:278-279 uses bits 26/27; the CMSIS header and the ST SVD both give FLASH_NSSR bits 18/19. The register guess (NSSR at offset 0x20, secure/src/hw/flash.rs:479) is right. The merge says the register and bits must be pinned on a sacrificial board; only the positive-detection half needs silicon.
3. **Leg 1 says nothing about secure-element state.** The transit attacker reads the OTP transport master over SWD without changing anything the tool checks, and so holds transport-level access to both SEs before first boot. The merge drops work item 3 of user-device-verification.md but never mentions work item 4 (seed wizard must delete and recreate SE state, never adopt it).
4. **Leg 1's hardware dependency is the time-critical part.** Without SWD and NRST reachable on the sealed unit, and without the panel lit by the FSBL (#705), no buyer can run the procedure. The P0 should be anchored on the ODM access decision, not on tool packaging.
5. **Leg 5 has an unflagged conflict.** An NS-callable C10 signer consumes a few-time key; bounding its use needs either a persistent counter (forbidden by "no new per-signature flash state beyond page 123") or a mandatory on-device confirm.
6. Several smaller factual errors in the live-defect wording, the option-byte read set, and the SE050 variant claim; see corrections.
skeptic.corrections:
**Leg 1 (verifier)**
- "Keep the WRITE_VERBS allow-list" is wrong: tools/verify_ship_state.py:53-74 is a deny-list of write verbs, despite the docstring. The new tool should use a real allow-list of read commands.
- The live-defect wording "its docstring says OTP is verified" overstates. Lines 4-6 quote invariant #10; the PROVES section (lines 23-24) honestly claims only option bytes and named flash regions. The defect is the gap between the invariant and the tool, not a false docstring.
- "Every option-byte register" then lists a subset. Add NSBOOTADD0/1, nBOOT0/nSWBOOT0, SWAP_BANK, TZEN, SECWM1R2/SECWM2R2 (HDP), the UNLOCK bit of each WRP register, and the SRAM ECC/erase bits.
- NRST: user-device-verification.md:184-186 says "No NRST needed (vector catch)", which lets firmware run from power-up until the probe halts it. The merge is right to require NRST; add that the tool cannot detect whether NRST was asserted before VBUS, so the procedure must order them, and that doc line needs fixing.
- The OTP "map" detects only added or changed quad-words. It cannot detect that the transport master (bytes 128..160) was read. State this as a residual: after any RDP-0 transit window the transport keys must be assumed known, so first-boot rotation secrecy rests on there being no bus tap. This ties to #76 (authenticate-before-rotate).
- Add the missing residual and work item: SE pre-state tampering. I found no explicit "never adopt" rule in secure/src/ui/seed_wizard.rs or secure/src/dual_se.rs by grep; that is a lead, not a confirmed gap.
- The NSSR check must use bits 18/19. Either correct lockdown.rs:278-279 with the vendor-header citation while keeping `OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED = false` until the bench positive detection, or record the correction in #46. If someone flips the pin flag without fixing the mask, the gate passes vacuously.

**Leg 2 (OEM key overwrite)**
- Prerequisite: fix #268 (use NSCR for OPTSTRT/OBL_LAUNCH/OPTLOCK) and add the OPTWERR check (flash.rs:560-563 leaves it unpinned). Trezor uses NSCR (option_bytes.c:230-237).
- It conflicts with the Phase A rule "verify, don't set — Phase A only ever writes the RDP byte" (secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:183-185). Compose it as: halt if a lock bit is set (existing 0x080A), then overwrite unconditionally in the burn as a belt against a skipped check. Do not silently heal a tampered unit. This needs an owner decision; the ship template's flow text says "heals option-byte drift", so the repo is inconsistent.
- Not verified here: whether RM0456 allows overwriting an already-set OEM1 key at RDP-0 without a mass erase. The Trezor comment implies yes.

**Leg 3 (birth record)**
- "E2/C2 decides whether attestation key 0xF0000012 exists" is overstated. #249 says C, E and F variants carry it and A/B/D do not; #697 is about which SCP03 keyset ships. Keep the variant-confirmation ask, drop the existence claim.
- The OPTIGA certificate OID is unconfirmed on this part: the repo records that 0xE0E3 is a full type-0x12 device certificate (secure/src/optiga/reset.rs:33, CLAUDE.md S-2), while the merge and #27 assume E0E0. Confirm on silicon which slot holds the Infineon certificate that pairs with E0F0. No E0E0/E0C2/E0F0 reader exists in secure/src.
- The privacy objection applied to UID96 applies equally to the SE UIDs, the E0E0 certificate and an E0F0 challenge-sign relay if they are NS-reachable before unlock. Gate them (first-boot only, or after unlock) or put them under the same owner privacy decision. A public log of UID tuples is a privacy surface too.
- The manifest "release and FSBL hash" is a factory claim; it must not be presented as firmware proof. Only leg 1 proves bytes.

**Leg 4 (bag serial)**
- The merge drops the FSBL-rendered serial as self-report at RDP-0, then keeps it on the secure-world lock-confirm page, which is equally self-report. Its only value is for a user who already ran leg 1, and the tool already prints it. Demote to P3, or keep it tool-only. build_lock_confirm_pages (secure/src/first_boot/state.rs:188-203) is a fixed const 2-page array, so a dynamic serial needs a new non-const builder.

**Leg 5 (CMD_ATTEST)**
- Add the signature-budget conflict above. At roughly 10 s per signature, a rate limit alone lets a host drive the key to the 65,536 cap in about a week. Require an on-device confirm; rate limiting alone is not enough.

live_defect.evidence:
Each merged live_defects entry, checked against the executing code. `usb` and `rdp2-self-lock` are both in PROD_SHIP_FEATURES (Makefile:2718).

1. GET_DEVICE_INFO placeholders: CONFIRMED. nonsecure/src/usb/commands.rs:178-182 (fixed FW_VERSION 3.0.0), :416 (16 zero bytes for device_uid), nonsecure/src/usb/mod.rs:199 (serial "0001"). Unconditional NS code in every `usb` build.

2. External verifier read set: CONFIRMED with one wording fix. tools/verify_ship_state.py:134-157 reads only option bytes and named flash hashes; the template profile is refused at :121-127. The docstring does not claim OTP is verified: lines 4-6 quote the invariant and lines 23-24 state the real scope. Also, WRITE_VERBS (:53-74) is a deny-list, not the allow-list the docstring and Makefile comment describe.

3. No OEM key reset: CONFIRMED. The only OEM symbols in Rust are the lock-bit masks in shared/src/lockdown.rs:278-279 and the status read at secure/src/hw/flash.rs:478-481; there is no OEMxKEYR write anywhere. `OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED = false` at lockdown.rs:290, so Phase A halts at 0x080A by design.

4. Wrong UID address in docs: CONFIRMED. CMSIS stm32u585xx.h:2098 gives UID_BASE 0x0BFA0700; secure/src/nsc/prodtest.rs:47 and proto/src/lib.rs:647,902 agree. docs/security/production-security.md:370,395,424 and the #249 body say 0x0BFA_0590, while production-security.md:140 says 0x0BFA_0700, so the doc contradicts itself.

5. Reproducible-build wording: CONFIRMED. docs/firmware/reproducible-builds.md:241 says every PR; .github/workflows/nightly.yml:130-145 is a nightly job; #456 is open.

Two defects the merge missed:

6. OEM-lock bit positions are wrong in code. shared/src/lockdown.rs:278-279 sets OEM1LOCK = 1<<26 and OEM2LOCK = 1<<27. The CMSIS header (STM32CubeU5 .../stm32u585xx.h:8668-8672) and the ST SVD (STM32CubeProgrammer/SVD/STM32U585.svd:6409-6421) give FLASH_NSSR bits 18 and 19. It fails closed today only because of the pin flag; flipping the flag without fixing the mask would pass a planted OEM key.

7. The RDP-2 burn is inert. secure/src/hw/flash.rs:384-394 documents defect #268 in place: OPTSTRT, OBL_LAUNCH and OPTLOCK are written to and read from FLASH_SECCR, where they do not exist, so program_rdp_level2_and_launch returns Ok without burning (:541-558). Leg 2 would inherit this.
live_defect.reachable_in_production_config: Entry 1: yes, in every `usb` build including PROD_SHIP_FEATURES. Entries 2, 4 and 5 are host tooling, docs and process.
